title: Multi Sensory Design
limitations: Methodological paper describing a design approach
No empirical study or quantitative data collection
Framework based on design experience and theory, not experimental validation
Examples are illustrative rather than evidence-based

extraction_metadata.notes: This paper presents the Multi Sensory Design (MSD) approach—an 8-step methodology for creating products that provide rich, integrated sensory experiences. It is not an empirical study and contains no quantitative findings or statistical analyses. The paper is prescriptive, describing a design process rather than reporting experimental results. It discusses how perceptual knowledge from all sensory modalities should be explicitly incorporated into design practice.
extraction_metadata.validation: JSON validated. No findings to extract—paper is methodological.

msd_approach_steps.name: Selecting the Target Expression
msd_approach_steps.description: Determine the expression the product should convey (e.g., eagerness, cheerfulness, innocence, safety, inspire). In business contexts, marketing may provide this; alternatively, designer determines desired effect on users.
msd_approach_steps.sensory_scope: Multi-modal (what expression means across all senses)

msd_approach_steps.name: Conceptual Exploration
msd_approach_steps.description: Develop understanding of the target expression through association and collage-making. What does the expression evoke?

msd_approach_steps.name: Sensory Exploration
msd_approach_steps.description: Collect samples evoking the target expression across all sensory modalities: pictures, materials, fragrances, fabrics, computer sounds, foods, plants. Explore non-obvious properties.

msd_approach_steps.name: Sensory Analysis
msd_approach_steps.description: Describe and understand relationships between perceived sensory properties and product expression. Why do certain samples relate to specific expression? What physical properties evoke it?

msd_approach_steps.name: Multisensory Mind Map
msd_approach_steps.description: Organize acquired information while maintaining richness. Center shows target expression; branches show main concepts; further branches show sensory dimensions. Maps descend from conceptual to concrete to sensory.

msd_approach_steps.name: User-Interaction Scenario
msd_approach_steps.description: Include time dimension. Describe user actions, product feedback, instructions, context. Identify sensory touchpoints throughout encounter (pickup, unwrap, use, store). Assess contribution to overall expression.

msd_approach_steps.name: Model Making
msd_approach_steps.description: Stay in physical materials; minimize visual sketching and digital modeling to avoid dominance by visual impressions. Sketch in all senses; assess appropriateness in proposed user context through collages and explorative physical models.

msd_approach_steps.name: Multisensory Presentation
msd_approach_steps.description: Communicate benefits through multisensory means. Show drawings, allow feeling foam models, present materials for touch and smell, play sound files. Use storyboards to show involvement of various senses in different interaction stages.

core_principles.description: Perceptual knowledge obtained through explorations in all sensory modalities is explicitly incorporated in design process
core_principles.rationale: Each sensory modality is sensitive to different energy types and stimulated by different product properties; modalities usually provide different pieces of product information

core_principles.description: Ultimate design challenge: develop product providing interesting, rich experience yet perceived as coherent whole
core_principles.rationale: Multisensory approach enriches product experience, avoids conflicting messages, results in products comprehensible for users with sensory impairments

core_principles.description: All sensory impressions must support expression of the product
core_principles.rationale: Bus stop example: may look attractive but be in cold breeze next to smelly trash with traffic noise; ice cream example: color, taste, texture, packaging, crispiness all contribute to immersion

core_principles.description: An expression can manifest itself in different ways
core_principles.rationale: Elegance example: may relate to flowing, uninterrupted movements but also to simple, straightforward solutions. Different sensory pathways can convey same expression.

core_principles.description: For branded products, brand associations can be added to mind map to ensure design contributes to brand image
core_principles.rationale: Parts of MSD approach may be modified or disregarded if conflicting with brand image
